input: Enroll in a free online ethics in AI course

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: AI ethics is a broad field — knowing whether the user wants a general overview or a specific subtopic (bias, fairness, governance, policy, etc.) determines which course fits best.
The user's professional background and familiarity with AI shapes which course level is appropriate — beginner, intermediate, or advanced.
Whether this is for personal growth, a job requirement, academic credit, or a certificate affects which platforms and course types are worth pursuing.
The user's available weekly time commitment determines whether a short micro-course or a multi-week structured course is realistic.
Preferred learning style — video lectures, readings, interactive exercises, or live sessions — narrows down the best platform and course format.
Whether the user needs a verifiable certificate of completion (vs. just the knowledge) changes which free courses qualify, since many platforms charge for certificates.
Platform preference or restrictions (e.g., Coursera, edX, LinkedIn Learning, YouTube) affects where to search and which enrollment steps to take next.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a free online AI ethics course
gold.taskDescription: Find and enroll in a free online course covering ethics in artificial intelligence.

questions.title: Which specific AI ethics topic interests you most?
questions.description: Identify whether the user wants a broad AI ethics overview or a focused subtopic such as algorithmic bias, data privacy, AI governance, or responsible AI design.

questions.title: What is your current level of AI knowledge?
questions.description: Determine if the user is a complete beginner, someone with general tech familiarity, or an AI/ML practitioner — to match the right course difficulty.

questions.title: What is your main reason for taking this course?
questions.description: Clarify whether the motivation is personal curiosity, career development, a job or academic requirement, or preparing for a specific role or project.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Establish the user's realistic time budget to filter between short self-paced modules (1-2 hrs) and longer structured courses (5+ hrs/week).

questions.title: Do you prefer video lectures, readings, or hands-on exercises?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred learning format to recommend courses on platforms that match their style — e.g., video-heavy (Coursera), reading-based (edX), or project-based.

questions.title: Do you need a shareable certificate when you finish?
questions.description: Determine if a verifiable certificate of completion is required, since many platforms offer free course access but charge for the certificate.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred learning platform already?
questions.description: Find out if the user has an existing account or preference for platforms like Coursera, edX, LinkedIn Learning, or is open to any option.
